# Capturefab

> A desktop app and command-line interface that captures camera images, video, sensor values and PLC tags for later analysis.

Capturefab runs on macOS, Windows and Linux.
It is for engineers who collect data on plant and OT networks.
Persons and scripts can use the same local camera session.
Signal sources use Modbus TCP, MQTT, OPC UA or MTConnect.
A DuckDB dataset catalogs saved files and signal samples.
Exports give Parquet or CSV files with a README and manifest for analysis tools.
Use the built-in simulators to try commands without camera or PLC hardware.

## Canonical resources

- [Documentation](docs.html): Task guides, app screenshots, installation and CLI reference.
- [Agent instructions](agents.md): Detailed automation contract, session behavior and recovery rules.
- [Camera compatibility](https://github.com/capturefab/capturefab/blob/main/docs/camera-compatibility.md): Transport requirements, camera profiles and unsupported paths.
- [Plant-floor guide](https://github.com/capturefab/capturefab/blob/main/docs/plant-floor.md): Templates, capture tags, signals, datasets, exports and FTP/SFTP destinations.
- [Workflow guide](https://github.com/capturefab/capturefab/blob/main/docs/cli-workflows.md): JSON plans, path resolution and partial failures.
- [Workflow examples](https://github.com/capturefab/capturefab/tree/main/examples/workflows): Multi-camera timelapse, scanner feeder and local recording.
- [Release manifest](releases.json): Published files, architectures, SHA-256 checksums and available signatures.
- [Release feed](feed.xml): Atom release announcements.
- [Source and build guide](https://github.com/capturefab/capturefab): Rust source, build instructions and MIT license.
- [FFmpeg build notes](https://github.com/capturefab/capturefab/blob/main/docs/ffmpeg-build.md): Media dependencies, corresponding source and build provenance.
- [Remote control](https://github.com/capturefab/capturefab/blob/main/docs/remote-control.md): Local browser interface and HTTP activity observation.

## Examine the installed version

The installed binary's schema and help output define its supported commands.

```sh
capturefab schema --json
capturefab doctor --json
capturefab sessions --json
capturefab --help
```

Capturefab opens its desktop app without a subcommand.
Use explicit subcommands for automation.
Every JSON data command uses a versioned envelope:

```json
{"version":1,"ok":true,"result":{}}
{"version":1,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"unavailable","message":"..."}}
```

Read the automation contract and CLI command tree from schema's `result`.
Plain `schema` prints the contract directly.
Data goes to stdout; diagnostics go to stderr.
Read the process exit code before you use the result.
Binary image stdout, raw XML, completions, help and version output use their command-specific formats.

Plain `doctor` checks the host and prints a fix for each warning.
`doctor --json` adds `host`, `efficiency`, `paths`, `limits`, `graphics` and `checks` (`{id,level,message,fix}`).
`--efficiency auto|smooth|efficient` or `CAPTUREFAB_EFFICIENCY` sets efficiency mode for a process and the camera workers it starts; `doctor` reports the mode in force and why.
Workers follow a change in their session's mode for decoders they start afterwards; efficient halves how often a session polls its workers for status.
Auto is efficient with at most 2 CPU cores or 2 GiB of memory, or in the OS low-power mode.
A headless build without a subcommand exits 5 and suggests `serve`.

Exit codes are 1 `operation_failed`, 2 `usage`, 3 `unavailable`, 4 `timeout`, 5 `unsupported` and 6 `storage_full`.
Capturefab rejects malformed supplied fields before connection and before capture/forward `--set` or `--auto` changes.
RPC and workflow commands reject unknown fields.
Valid feature writes run in order; a later live failure does not reverse earlier writes.

## Use an existing session

Camera commands, discovery and network scans automatically use the only active authenticated desktop or `serve` session.
With several sessions, specify `--session NAME`.
With no session, supported camera commands use a temporary worker.
Use `--direct --camera ID` to select a temporary worker explicitly.
`--direct` overrides `CAPTUREFAB_SESSION` and conflicts with an explicit `--session` option.

```sh
capturefab gui --name bench
# In another terminal:
capturefab --session bench connect sim:0
capturefab --session bench --camera sim:0 get Width Height --json
capturefab --session bench --camera sim:0 capture -o first.png --json
capturefab --session bench status --json
```

`CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA` supplies a default source; `CAPTUREFAB_SESSION` supplies a default session.
`--camera ID` targets a camera and keeps each desktop or browser participant's local selection.
`select ID` sets the default for CLI calls without `--camera`.
Persistent `start` and `auto` controls act on a connected camera; use `connect ID` first.
Binary stdout captures use a temporary worker and cannot use `--session`.
Camera control can be exclusive, so use the existing session for an open camera.

`--timeout-ms` limits each frame or transport operation to 1–60000 ms.
`--request-timeout 5m` limits the full session request.
Its default depends on the capture count.
A client timeout does not cancel an accepted session command.
Read status and Activity before you retry a write.

## Observe shared work

Commands for one camera run in order.
Separate cameras operate independently; overlapping schedules share acquisition.
Use `--actor NAME --actor-kind agent` for an automation agent.
`CAPTUREFAB_ACTOR` and `CAPTUREFAB_ACTOR_KIND` provide defaults; the default kind is `human`.
Actor metadata is display attribution, not authentication.

In `status --json`, `lost` counts frames lost on the camera link or in the worker; use it for acquisition health. `preview_skipped` counts preview frames a viewer missed because a newer one was ready. `dropped` keeps its v1 meaning: worker receive errors plus `preview_skipped`.
Analytics (`/api/analytics`, the charts and `/metrics`) count missed frames as `lost`; totals and cameras add `lost` and `preview_skipped`, Prometheus adds `capturefab_{session,camera}_lost_frames_total` and `capturefab_{session,camera}_preview_skipped_frames_total`, and `samples` counts one-second samples of all cameras together, so 24 hours fit for any camera count.

`status --json` includes global `result.activity` and `result.activity_revision`, even for a busy target camera.
Activity retains the latest 200 completed entries plus active commands and schedules.
Sequences include `file_count` and at most eight path previews; capture results still return the full file list.
`target_camera` identifies the requested camera; `active_camera` identifies the session default.
A successful schedule command confirms job creation; inspect its `job` for completion or failure.
A successful forwarding command confirms encoder startup; inspect camera status for continued forwarding.

```sh
capturefab --session bench activity --json
capturefab --session bench activity --after 12 --wait 20s --json
```

Activity responses contain `{revision,activity}` inside the versioned result.
These read-only calls bypass camera queues and create no Activity entries.
RPC supports `{"op":"activity","after":12,"timeout_ms":20000}`.
HTTP observers use `/api/activity?after=REV&timeout_ms=20000`; the maximum timeout is 25000 ms.
All observers wake on shared command and scheduled-job changes.
See the agent instructions for actor fields, log timestamps and HTTP command envelopes.

## Capture, save and record

Local CLI/RPC paths use the directory of the terminal that sends the command.
Saved destination output names are relative to that destination.
Existing output files are not overwritten.
Single-file and template extensions select PNG, JPEG, raw, PGM or PPM.
Directory sequences default to PNG; `--format` overrides format selection.
Capture paths do not accept network URLs.
See "Name and tag captures" for templates and numbering.

Durations and timestamp fractions must resolve to whole milliseconds.
`1.001s` is valid; `1.1ms` fails.
All scheduled frames must occur within 10 years.
Keep the GUI, headless session or direct command active for the schedule lifetime.

`record` is an alias for `forward`.
`record --duration 30s` keeps the CLI active and stops the encoder at the deadline or Ctrl-C.
This works with temporary workers and persistent sessions.
Without a duration, a session command returns immediately and records until `stop-forward`.
A direct recording command stays active until Ctrl-C.
`stop-forward` returns final `stats`: `accepted`, `written`, `dropped`, `late`, `stalled`, `encoder`, `error`; `record --duration` adds them as `stopped`.
`late` counts frames lost while the encoder was busy; `stalled` means no new camera frame for 2 s.
Recordings keep wall-clock time, so a file lasts as long as its recording and a camera stall leaves a gap.
H.265 or AV1 without a working hardware encoder fails before recording with exit 5 and names the working codecs.
Network stream sources reconnect by themselves, backing off from 1 s to 30 s; frame waits meanwhile time out (exit 4). Only repeated credential rejections stop them.
Video file sources play at their frame rate in live view; captures that start acquisition read them as fast as they ask; `PlaybackSpeed=Fastest` decodes every frame as fast as possible.

Saved destinations include folders, external drives, network folders, S3-compatible buckets, FTP/FTPS servers and SFTP servers.
Use `destination list --json`, `volumes --json` and `uploads --json` to inspect them.
Credentials use the operating system keychain, AWS profiles or process environment.
SFTP destinations must have a pinned host key: `--host-key SHA256:...` or `--accept-host-key`.
`add-s3 --preset rustfs` or `--preset minio` must have `--endpoint`.
A remote file is never replaced; FTP rename can replace on some servers, so use one writer per FTP folder.
Persistent sessions return local capture results before upload completion; inspect the upload queue.
`uploads --json` has `destinations:{NAME:{pending,uploading,failed,waiting_bytes,next_attempt,last_error}}` over every queued upload; `next_attempt` is in Unix seconds.
A failing destination backs off as a whole for uploads it already tried, while new ones still go ahead; `uploads retry --now` retries waiting uploads at once, and `uploads retry` retries failed ones at once.
An item queued while the storage ledger was busy has `unheld:true` until the uploader holds it back from retention.

Captures and recordings share a storage budget across processes with the same `CAPTUREFAB_SESSION_DIR`.
Defaults are 10 GiB and 10,000 files; each recording defaults to a 512 MiB file limit.
Use `storage --json` to inspect usage and reservations; `free_bytes` is the free space on the default capture folder's disk.
Every save must leave 512 MiB free on its disk, counting what active recordings may still write.
A storage-full error has exit code 6.
You must have explicit user authorization for retention deletion or an increased global budget.

## Name and tag captures

Capture and local recording outputs accept a file, a directory or a template.
Placeholders are `{camera}`, `{date}`, `{time}`, `{datetime}`, `{seq}` and `{frame}`.
`{seq}` selects the next free number for that folder and pattern.
`{camera}` is the sanitized model and serial, never the address.
Times use local time when the frame is requested.
Other placeholders cause a usage error (exit 2).

```sh
capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -o 'line1/{date}/{camera}-{datetime}-{seq}.png' --json
capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -o shot.png --on-exists number --json
capturefab --camera sim:0 capture -o 'qa/{camera}-{seq}.png' --context line=L1 --context part=A-100 --json
```

`--on-exists fail` is the CLI and RPC default.
`--on-exists number` writes `stem-0001.ext`, `stem-0002.ext` and so on.
A directory output continues its `frame-NNNNNN` numbers.
`--context KEY=VALUE` tags captures and recordings; keys match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$`.
Read saved names from `result.files` and `result.frames[].file`.
`frames[].wall_ms` is UTC milliseconds.
A recording result gives the resolved file in `path` and the start time in `since_ms`.
The desktop saves to `~/Capturefab/{date}/{camera}-{datetime}-{seq}.png` by default.

## Read sensors and PLCs

```sh
capturefab signals read sim-signal://line1 --json
capturefab signals browse opc.tcp://HOST:4840 --duration 5s --json
capturefab log sim-signal://line1 --duration 10m --dataset plant.duckdb --csv line1.csv --json
capturefab --session bench signals start 'modbus-tcp://HOST/1/holding/0?type=f32&name=temp_c' --json
capturefab --session bench signals --json
capturefab --session bench signals stop all --json
```

URI schemes are `modbus-tcp://`, `mqtt://`, `mqtts://`, `opc.tcp://`, `mtconnect://`, `mtconnects://` and `sim-signal://`.
Read `result.signals.uris` in `schema --json` for the full syntax.
Modbus addresses are 0-based; Modicon 40001 is `holding/0`.
OPC UA uses SecurityPolicy None only, so passwords travel unencrypted.
Capturefab removes credentials from all output.
`signals start` and `signals stop` must have a running GUI or `serve` session.
`log` must have `--csv`, `--dataset` or both.
Browse is unsupported for Modbus (exit 5).
Each source runs in a separate helper process and restarts a maximum of 5 times.
A session holds a maximum of 16 sources.
`ts_ms` is the host clock in UTC milliseconds; `source_ts_ms` is the device clock.
Capturefab reads signal values; it does not write to devices.

## Catalog and export datasets

```sh
capturefab --session bench dataset open /data/plant.duckdb --json
capturefab --session bench dataset note "nozzle changed" --context line=L1 --json
capturefab --session bench dataset query "SELECT * FROM captures_with_signals LIMIT 20" --json
capturefab --session bench dataset export -o /data/exports/shift-b --json
capturefab dataset query --file /data/plant.duckdb "SELECT count(*) FROM captures" --json
```

One `.duckdb` file is one dataset, owned by one session.
`--dataset FILE.duckdb` on `capture`, `record`, `serve`, `gui` and `log` creates or opens it.
Tables are `captures`, `recordings`, `signals`, `samples` and `events`.
The `captures_with_signals` view joins each capture with the latest sample of each tag.
Every `*_ms` column is UTC Unix milliseconds; `context` is JSON text.
Queries accept one read-only SELECT or WITH statement and return at most 10,000 rows.
`--file` on a dataset that a session holds fails with exit 3; use `--session`.
Exports go to a new folder: Parquet and CSV files, `manifest.json` and `README.md`.
Give the export `README.md` and `manifest.json` to an analysis model first.
An existing export folder fails with exit 1; a full storage budget fails with exit 6 before writing.
RPC operations are `dataset_open`, `dataset_close`, `dataset_status`, `dataset_note`, `dataset_query` and `dataset_export`.
Signal RPC operations are `signals`, `signal_read`, `signal_browse`, `signal_start` and `signal_stop`.
Workflow files can use these operations too.

## Learn automatic captures

```sh
capturefab --session bench --camera sim:0 capture-session new line.duckdb --json
capturefab --session bench --camera sim:0 capture-session teach --json
capturefab --session bench --camera sim:0 capture-session auto --sensitivity 0.5 --json
capturefab --session bench --camera sim:0 capture-session review --json
capturefab --session bench --camera sim:0 capture-session keep 2 --json
```

A capture session is one camera-bound `.duckdb` file; it needs a running GUI or `serve` session and a connected camera.
`teach` captures positive examples; `keep` and `discard` label pending suggestions. Pending suggestions never train.
`new --encoder auto` (the default) uses the DINOv2 ViT-S/14 model bundled in the executable; nothing is downloaded.
Embeddings run on the GPU in an isolated helper process when possible (up to 30 frames per second), otherwise on the CPU.
`status --json` reports `capture_session.accelerator` and `samples_per_second`; `doctor --json` reports `auto_capture.dinov2.gpu`.
`--encoder native` uses a color/edge descriptor; `CAPTUREFAB_DINOV2_GPU=0` keeps DINOv2 on the CPU.
A session keeps its encoder and model fingerprint: `resume` refuses a session learned with a different bundled model (exit 1).
RPC operations are `capture_session_open` (`path`, `create`, optional `encoder`), `capture_session_close`, `capture_example`, `auto_capture`, `capture_review` and `review_capture`.

## Apply workflow files

```sh
capturefab workflow validate workflow.json --json
capturefab workflow apply workflow.json --dry-run --json
capturefab --session bench workflow apply workflow.json --json
```

Validation and dry runs are offline.
Documents use `{version:1,steps:[{camera?:ID,command:SessionCommand}]}`.
They accept 1–256 steps and a maximum size of 1 MiB.
Connect/select use `command.camera`; omit their outer camera target.
Discovery and network scans also omit the outer target.
All steps pass offline validation before execution; device and destination availability remain execution checks.
Apply must use a persistent session and cannot use global `--camera`.

Workflow paths use the JSON file's directory; stdin input uses the calling terminal's directory.
Local `file:`, `sim:replay:` and existing media inputs use those directories too.
Steps stop at the first failure and keep earlier effects.
Read `error.details.completed`, `completed_steps` and `failed_step` before recovery.
Schedules and encoders continue in the session after Apply exits.
Workflow commands have no duration or wait field; use timed CLI recording or separate start/stop files.

## Change camera settings

Read the current feature list, choices, access permissions and limits before a write.
Read back important values after a write.
Auto exposure is optional for each camera.
Use `auto --balance 0..1` and `manual [--revert]` in a session.
A balance of 0 favors image quality; 1 favors frame rate.
Ask before you enable Auto on a camera that other software uses.

`history`, `undo` and `redo` expose reversible settings for each connected camera.
GUI, CLI and RPC clients share this limited history.
Captures, uploads, recordings, schedules, connections, arbitrary commands and raw memory writes cannot use camera Undo.
Scanner settings are reversible; scanner acquisition can move physical pages and cannot use Undo.

`network-scan --json` inspects IPv4 interfaces and GigE cameras, then tunes available connected cameras within a shared interface budget.
The scan can briefly pause previews for packet probes.
Active recordings, forwarding or schedules prevent tuning.
It does not change host IP addresses, routes or MTUs.
See the agent instructions for network health values and RPC fields.

## Camera types and limits

Identity JSON includes `profile:{kind,source,evidence,capabilities}`.
Profile kinds are unknown, area scan, line scan, depth, microscope, thermal and document scanner.
Detection does not certify physical compatibility or writable controls.
The interface uses advertised features to adapt its control groups and previews.

Typed simulators are `sim:line`, `sim:depth`, `sim:microscope` and `sim:thermal`, with optional `:name` suffixes.
`sim:0` and other ordinary names supply area-scan images.
Simulators exercise software behavior; they do not prove hardware compatibility.

Line-scan captures save individual blocks; the preview history is not a full reconstructed scan.
Depth and thermal preview colors show raw sample ranges without measurement calibration.
For measurements, use `capture --format raw` and retain dimensions, pixel format, component, units, scale, offset and calibration metadata separately.
Raw files do not embed that metadata.
PNG, JPEG, PGM, PPM and forwarded video are 8-bit display outputs.
Depth sources must supply a compatible single-component image stream.
Multipart, GenDC, point-cloud payloads and vendor SDK-only access are unsupported.
Generic auto exposure is unsupported for line scan, depth, thermal and document scanners.

Scanners use full `scanner:sane:DEVICE`, `scanner:wia:ID` or `scanner:ica:UUID` identifiers.
Linux must have SANE scanimage/backends; Windows uses WIA and Windows PowerShell; macOS uses an included ImageCaptureCore helper.
Use `--timeout-ms 60000` for CLI page captures.
Each capture requests one page; successive pages save as separate images.
Driver compatibility has not been physically validated.
Scanner sources do not provide PDF assembly, OCR, forwarding or auto exposure.

## Choose a release

Release data determines the available downloads.
An empty release array means that no binary downloads are published.
Match the installed operating system and architecture.
A Macintosh browser user-agent string does not identify Apple silicon or Intel reliably.
See the installation guide for extraction steps and operating system minimums.
